  WHY: The deferred filer selects only rows with `followup_pending`, while later audits suppress findings matched by the recorded waiver; severity differed (NIT/MAJOR), so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1977-2029 | severity=high | confidence=[4]

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6560 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]

  WHY: The per-finding full-state update repeats work as the number of advisories grows.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7298, 7804 | severity=low | confidence=[2]

  PROBLEM: The exhaustion-judge-path `SECURITY_PASS_CLEAN` log omits the trailing `advisory=<n>` field present in the main-path log.
  WHY: Tooling that expects `advisory=` on every `SECURITY_PASS_CLEAN` line will miss advisory counts from exhaustion-judge clean passes.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6555-6570 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: When both `create_security_pass_advisory_followup` and the subsequent `jq` state-update fail, the waiver row stays with `issue: null` and no `followup_pending` marker.
  WHY: The deferred filer selects only rows where `followup_pending == true`, and the next audit suppresses the finding via the already-recorded waiver, so the advisory follow-up is never filed and no retry path remains.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6560 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Each advisory finding executes a full `jq` over `security_pass_waived_findings` to set `followup_pending`.
  WHY: With many advisories needing the marker, the per-tick jq cost grows quadratically and slows the poller tick.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1977-2029 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Every finding gets its own `git blame` invocation, one subprocess per finding.
  WHY: Hundreds of sequential blame calls can make the path slow; the per-call timeout bounds total wall time, but this is the slowest possible pattern.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7298, 7804 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The exhaustion-judge-path `SECURITY_PASS_CLEAN` log omits an `advisory=<n>` trailing field that the main-path log includes.
  WHY: Downstream tooling that expects `advisory=` on every `SECURITY_PASS_CLEAN` line can miss exhaustion-judge advisory counts.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
